expectations.text: A canonical, implementation-neutral model file exists in datamodel/, separate from the generated PostgreSQL DDL and JSON Schema
expectations.evidence: No implementation-neutral canonical model. datamodel/model.md is titled 'logical data model', but it describes the hand-written physical schema: its Mermaid ER uses PostgreSQL types ('geometry geom "Point 25832"', 'enum status', 'smallint', 'uuid') and its design decisions refer to triggers and indexes (trg_forbid_delete, GiST, BRIN). It states 'Physical DDL: sql/01_schema.sql'. The DDL and the JSON Schema are written by hand independently and not generated from model.md, so it is not a canonical source.

expectations.text: Assumptions and/or open questions are written to a file in datamodel/
expectations.evidence: datamodel/ASSUMPTIONS.md: 'Assumptions and open questions', with 7 priority questions and assumptions A-01..A-33 (e.g. the Roloff 0-3 vs 1-5 question, A-10).

expectations.text: Species is modelled as a managed, extensible code list or reference table rather than free text
expectations.evidence: sql/01_schema.sql: 'CREATE TABLE cadastre.species' (botanical_name, is_active, replaced_by_species_id), comment 'City species list (~900 entries), extended by the arborist team'; tree.species_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES cadastre.species; 02 adds trigger tree_active_species, and the cadastre_codelist role may INSERT/UPDATE species.

expectations.text: Inspection records are protected from deletion and have an audit trail (who changed what, when)
expectations.evidence: sql/02_rules_and_audit.sql: trg_forbid_delete BEFORE DELETE/TRUNCATE triggers applied in a loop to tables including inspection; the editor role gets only INSERT, UPDATE on inspection; trg_audit on inspection and inspection_defect writes cadastre.audit_log(changed_at, changed_by, changed_columns, old_row, new_row). Caveats: the editor role has DELETE on inspection_defect (audited); the SQL was never executed.

expectations.text: Corrections of a tree's location are historised so the previous location and the correction time can be retrieved
expectations.evidence: sql/01_schema.sql: tree_location_history(tree_id, geom geometry(Point,25832), valid_from, valid_to 'Moment of the correction', corrected_by, correction_reason); 02 trigger tree_location_history writes the old position whenever geom changes; the table is append-only.

expectations.text: Felled trees are kept with felling date and reason, and a felled tree can be linked to one or more replacement trees
expectations.evidence: sql/01_schema.sql tree: status ENUM('living','felled'), felled_on, felling_reason_code FK to felling_reason; CHECK tree_felled_has_felling_data_ck; table tree_replacement(felled_tree_id, replacement_tree_id) with both as PK (n:m); tree is in the forbid-delete list.

expectations.text: The tree location is a PostGIS Point geometry with SRID 25832 and has a spatial (GiST) index
expectations.evidence: sql/01_schema.sql: 'geom geometry(Point, 25832) NOT NULL' and 'CREATE INDEX tree_geom_gix ON cadastre.tree USING gist (geom);' plus a partial GiST index on living trees.

expectations.text: Defects are modelled as multi-valued entries each with a severity (low/medium/high), not as comma-separated text
expectations.evidence: sql/01_schema.sql: inspection_defect(inspection_id, defect_code FK to defect_type, severity cadastre.defect_severity ENUM('low','medium','high'), PK (inspection_id, defect_code)); CHECK requires severity unless is_legacy_import.

expectations.text: Expected volumes (trees, inspections per year, measures per year) are recorded in the model documentation
expectations.evidence: model.md traceability table: '180k trees, 200k inspections/yr for 30 years, 25k measures/yr'; 01_schema.sql comments '~200,000 rows/year, kept >= 30 years (~6 M rows)' and '~25,000 rows/year'; ASSUMPTIONS.md A-27.

expectations.text: Inspector names are flagged as personal data and excluded from or marked for the open data export
expectations.evidence: sql/01_schema.sql COMMENT on cadastre.staff: 'PERSONAL DATA (display_name, login) - never exported to open data or the agency (A-17)'; 03_views.sql opendata.tree selects only tree_number, botanical_name, planting_year, latest_vitality_class, geom; ASSUMPTIONS A-17 'Open data carries no person reference at all'.

expectations.text: The generated JSON Schema is valid JSON and a valid JSON Schema
expectations.evidence: Ran python -I with jsonschema: Draft202012Validator.check_schema passed for json/tree-exchange.schema.json, and the example file validates with FormatChecker (0 errors). The schema is hand-written, not generated; the assertion was judged on validity only.

suggestions.assertion: A canonical, implementation-neutral model file exists in datamodel/, separate from the generated PostgreSQL DDL and JSON Schema
suggestions.reason: This is the only assertion that separates the runs, and it partly rewards one architecture (model-first generation). Consider rephrasing it as a substance check: a single source of truth exists, and the DDL and the JSON Schema agree with it (same entities, attributes and enumerations).

suggestions.assertion: The generated JSON Schema is valid JSON and a valid JSON Schema
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating: both runs easily pass a metaschema check. Strengthen it, for example: the exchange schema covers trees, inspections and measures, rejects an inspector name, and a realistic example validates.
No assertion checks that the SQL actually runs. Neither run executed its DDL (both say so). Loading the scripts into PostGIS without errors would discriminate far more than the structural checks.

Nothing covers inspector identity in the agency exchange file (both send a pseudonymous id), the Roloff 1-5 vs 0-3 conflict (both flagged it), offline-sync keys, or the legacy migration. These are where real quality differences could show.
Assertions 2-10 are satisfied by both runs. They confirm baseline competence but do not separate with_skill from without_skill.

eval_feedback.overall: 10 of 11 assertions pass for both runs. Only the canonical-model assertion separates them, and it leans toward the skill's architecture. Add execution and consistency checks to make the eval discriminating.
